cards.explanation: The answer is Aaron and his sons alone. God says, “…you and your sons alone must bear the iniquity involving your priesthood.” That word "alone" is doing the heavy lifting here, friends. This part of the job doesn't get passed around the camp. It stays in Aaron's family. (Num 18:1)

The word is "assist." God says the Levites will join Aaron and assist him and his sons before the Tent of the Testimony. ASSIST, friends! Helpers don't get enough credit. I'm a cookie stamper with a mustache for hands, and even I need the help. (Num 18:2)

The answer is the furnishings of the sanctuary and the altar. God says the Levites "…must not come near to the furnishings of the sanctuary or the altar, or both they and you will die." The Levites have plenty to do around the Tent, but those two things are off limits to them. Notice the "you" there too, friends, because Aaron is part of what's at stake. (Num 18:3)

The answer is False. God says, “…or both they and you will die.” He's talking to Aaron there, so Aaron is included along with the Levites. It's a heavy line, and the text doesn't soften it. (Num 18:3)

The answer is so that wrath may not fall on the Israelites again. God says the purpose of Aaron's duties at the sanctuary and the altar is "…so that wrath may not fall on the Israelites again." That "again" is a heavy word, friends. I think it points back to what the Israelites just went through, and it tells me this job matters a great deal. (Num 18:5)

The word is "gift." God says, “…I Myself have selected your fellow Levites from the Israelites as a gift to you, dedicated to the LORD to perform the service for the Tent of Meeting.” Aaron gets a whole crew handed to him. I got a 25-cent price sticker and a junk drawer. I'm only a little jealous. (Num 18:6)

The answer is True. God says it straight: “I am giving you the work of the priesthood as a gift…” That's the same word He used for the Levites. So the work itself is a gift to Aaron and his sons. God hands them a heavy job and still calls it a gift. (Num 18:7)

The answer is that they must be put to death. God says, “…any outsider who comes near the sanctuary must be put to death.” This one is heavy. Right before it, God says only Aaron and his sons shall attend to the priesthood, everything concerning the altar and what is inside the veil. That work is theirs, and God gives it to them as a gift. (Num 18:7)

The answer is the LORD Himself. God tells Aaron, “I am your portion and your inheritance among the Israelites.” Aaron gets no inheritance in their land and no portion among them. What he gets is God Himself. I think that's the best inheritance in the whole passage, friends. (Num 18:20)

The word is "tithes." God says, “Behold, I have given to the Levites all the tithes in Israel as an inheritance in return for the work they do…” The Levites get no land among the Israelites, so the tithes are their inheritance. That's their pay for serving at the Tent of Meeting. (Num 18:21, 23)

The answer is that they will incur guilt and die. God says, “No longer may the Israelites come near to the Tent of Meeting, or they will incur guilt and die.” That's a heavy line. The work at the Tent belongs to the Levites and the priests. (Num 18:22)

The answer is a tithe of the tithe. God tells Moses, Israel's leader, to say to the Levites, “…you must present part of it as an offering to the LORD—a tithe of the tithe.” God has Moses pass the instruction to the Levites. The Levites receive the tithe, and they give a tithe of it back. (Num 18:25–26)

The answer is Aaron the priest. God tells Moses to speak to the Levites: "…from these you are to give the LORD’s offering to Aaron the priest." The Israelites give the tithe to the Levites, and then the Levites hand part of it up to Aaron. So the Levites receive AND give. That's a whole line of hands passing things along, and I love to see it. (Num 18:28)

The word is "best." God says, “You must present the offering due the LORD from all the best of every gift, the holiest part of it.” The Levites give from the top shelf, not from what's left over. A cookie box for a celebration gets the good batch, friends. (Num 18:29)

The answer is False. God says, “And you and your households may eat the rest of it anywhere; it is the compensation for your work at the Tent of Meeting.” The Levites can eat it anywhere, and their households can share it. (Num 18:31)

The answer is that they will die. The passage ends with a heavy line: “But you must not defile the sacred offerings of the Israelites, or else you will die.” The Levites have been given a big job, and the sacred offerings are to be treated as sacred. I think that's a weighty way to end, friends. (Num 18:32)
